newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.C. Giuliani's approval ratings firm - survey.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.C. Giuliani's approval ratings firm - survey.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani's approval rating rose four percentage points to 54-38 percent, while the Bronx Borough president has the best chance to beat him in a race, a poll said on Friday.

The Quinnipiac College Poll said the city's races remain sharply divided in their evaluations of Giuliani, who is approved of by 68-23 percent of whites and 54-41 percent of Hispanics. But 25-66 percent of the blacks who were polled give him a negative rating.

The poll, which has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.6 percent, showed that Bronx Borough President Fernando Ferrer would lose to Giuliani in a theoretical race by 47-39 percent, with 14 percent undecided.
But Ferrer did better than other potential contendors, as shown by the following list of potential match-ups.
--49-40 percent over Manhattan Borough President Ruth Messinger.
--48-34 percent over City Comptroller Alan Hevesi.
--53-27 percent over City Council Member Sal Albanese.
Giuliani, whose overall rating last was measured in July, still gets his best marks for handling crime, enjoying a 76-20 percent rating.

While the 733 New York City residents who were surveyed gave him lower marks for his welfare policies, they still approved of them by 50-37 percent. But they gave the mayor a negative rating on education of 34-56 percent.
The mayor's handling of the budget defict also was dispproved, though by a narrower margin of 41-46 percent.
